verdict.rationale: Google Cloud's free page documents both parts of the story: $300 in free credit for new customers with no charge until a paid account is activated, and an always-free tier of products (AI APIs, Compute Engine, BigQuery) up to monthly limits that does not count against the credit. The evidence only states that 'specified' or monthly limits exist and never gives the actual figures or any expiry for the credit. Missing for 10: expiry period of the $300 credit, concrete per-product free-tier limits, a published startup credits program, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, starting is free — an always-free tier and/or published startup credits with the limits and expiry spelled out

citations.quote: New customers get $300 in free credit to try Google Cloud products and build a proof of concept. You won't be charged until you activate your full paid account.
There is no charge to use these products up to their specified free usage limit.
Get free usage of AI APIs, Compute Engine, BigQuery, and other popular products up to monthly limits—not charged against your $300 free credit.
